topic: speed per gear and sprocket effect
statement: With stock 13/51 gearing and the stock 110/100-18 rear tire, road speed per 1,000 rpm works out to about 1: 2.5 mph, 2: 3.3 mph, 3: 4.2 mph, 4: 5.3 mph, 5: 6.3 mph, 6: 7.4 mph. One more tooth on the rear sprocket makes every gear about 2.0% shorter; one less on the front about 8.3% shorter.

vals.gear_1: 2.5 mph (4.1 km/h) per 1,000 rpm; overall ratio 31.37:1
vals.gear_2: 3.3 mph (5.4 km/h) per 1,000 rpm; overall ratio 23.84:1
vals.gear_3: 4.2 mph (6.7 km/h) per 1,000 rpm; overall ratio 19.00:1
vals.gear_4: 5.3 mph (8.5 km/h) per 1,000 rpm; overall ratio 15.03:1
vals.gear_5: 6.3 mph (10.1 km/h) per 1,000 rpm; overall ratio 12.58:1
vals.gear_6: 7.4 mph (11.9 km/h) per 1,000 rpm; overall ratio 10.72:1

notes: Worked out from Yamaha's published primary ratio 3.353, gearbox ratios and final drive 13/51: speed = rpm / (primary x gear x final) x tire circumference. Tire rolling diameter is estimated from the size code (rim 18 in + 2 x 110 mm x 100%) = 677 mm; a knobby under load rolls slightly smaller, so real speeds run a little lower. Multiply by rpm/1,000 for a given engine speed.

statement: Yamaha's tuning chart for this model says: set rear sag (sunken length 90-100 mm) first; if the fork is stiff over its whole range back the compression out about 2 clicks, take 5-10 cc of oil out or fit a softer spring; if it is soft and bottoms, add about 2 clicks of compression or 5-10 cc of oil, or fit a stiffer spring; change oil in 5 cc steps for end-of-stroke feel. After a softer spring go 1-2 clicks out on rebound, after a stiffer one 1-2 clicks in.

statement: Yamaha's troubleshooting chart for the 2024 YZ250FX traces hard starting, poor idle and poor mid-to-high-speed running to: a clogged or failing fuel pump, a failed or clogged injector, a blocked tank-cap breather, stale or contaminated fuel, wrong valve timing, valve clearance out of spec, a bent or stuck valve, a tired or broken valve spring, a worn cam lobe, a dirty throttle body, a cracked throttle-body joint (air leak), engine oil overfilled, the wrong oil grade letting the starter clutch slip, besides ignition faults (no spark).

causes_listed: a clogged or failing fuel pump
a tired or broken valve spring
the wrong oil grade letting the starter clutch slip

notes: Troubleshooting chapter (TROUBLESHOOTING OF ENGINE). Yamaha notes the chart is a quick-reference guide and does not cover every cause.

topic: 2024 YZ250FX Yamaha clutch, gearbox and cooling troubleshooting

overheating: carbon build-up in the combustion chamber

notes: Troubleshooting chapter (clutch, transmission and cooling system tables).

topic: 2024 YZ250FX what a sprocket change does
statement: Worked out from the 2024 YZ250FX stock 13/51 gearing: each rear tooth changes every gear by about 2.0% and one front tooth by about 7.7% (one front tooth is roughly 3.9 rear teeth). Yamaha's 47T to 52T rear range spans final ratios 3.615 to 4.000 (stock 3.923), so the 47T gives about +8.5% road speed per rpm in every gear and the 52T about -1.9%: more teeth means shorter gearing, quicker pull and a lower top speed.
notes: Percent per tooth = 1/teeth; final ratio = rear/front teeth.

statement: Yamaha's 2024 lineup announcement lists the YZ250FX among the cross-country models that return for 2024 with updated graphics and a new seat color; unlike the 2024 YZ250F it received no engine or frame update, so it keeps the previous-generation YZ250FX engine and chassis.
notes: The spec tables of the 2022 (BAJ-2819U-12), 2023 (BAJ-2819U-13) and 2024 (BAJ-2819U-14) US owner service manuals were compared: engine, gearing, suspension and chassis figures are identical (only a clutch friction-plate wear limit differs, 2.60 vs 2.62 mm, and text formatting).

source.name: Yamaha Motor Corporation USA press release "Yamaha Celebrates 50 Years of YZ" (2024 lineup)

statement: A rear-wheel dyno test of the 2022 YZ250FX, mechanically identical to the 2024, measured 37.9 hp at 12,100 rpm and 18.3 lb-ft of torque at 8,800 rpm; peak power was up only 0.1 hp on the 2021 bike, with peak torque the same but arriving 400 rpm later.
notes: Tested bike is a 2022. Applied to 2024 because Yamaha says the 2024 FX carries over with graphics only and the 2022-2024 manual spec tables match (see identity record). Dyno model and map not stated; in-house dyno, rear street tire. No dyno test of a 2023 or 2024 FX was found.

source.name: Dirt Rider, 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX Dyno Test (Andrew Oldar)

topic: 2024 YZ250FX tire pressure and fork oil level by conditions
statement: Yamaha's tuning chapter sets standard tire pressure at 100 kPa (15 psi), dropping to 60-80 kPa (9-12 psi) for rain, mud, sand or slippery ground and raising it to 100-120 kPa (15-18 psi) for stony or hard ground to avoid flats. The fork's end-of-stroke (air spring) feel is tuned with the oil level: standard 295 cm³, adjustable from 260 to 365 cm³ in 5 cm³ steps; too little gives a clunk at full extension, too much makes the end of the stroke harsh.
notes: Tuning chapter 10-1 and 10-2.

source.name: Yamaha 2024 YZ250FX Owner's Service Manual (BAJ-2819U-14)

topic: 2024 YZ250FX shock spring options and set-up after a spring change
statement: Yamaha lists optional shock springs from 48 to 60 N/mm in 2 N/mm steps (standard 56 N/mm) and fork springs from 4.1 to 5.1 N/mm (standard 4.6). After fitting any shock spring, reset sag to a 90-100 mm sunken (rider-on) length; with a softer spring turn rebound out 1-2 clicks, with a stiffer one turn it in 1-2 clicks, and since rebound changes affect compression feel, back compression off to correct. Recheck sag once a new spring has bedded in.
notes: Tuning chapter 10-3/10-4 (rear shock absorber and front fork setting parts tables, choosing set length).

source.name: Yamaha 2024 YZ250FX Owner's Service Manual (BAJ-2819U-14)

topic: 2024 YZ250FX Power Tuner fuel and ignition changes
statement: Fuel and ignition can be changed without parts using Yamaha's Power Tuner smartphone app, which writes injection and ignition-timing corrections into the ECU and selects which map the handlebar mode switch calls up. A dealer diagnostic tool can show whether Power Tuner settings are stored (diagnostic codes 60 and 64) and erase all setting maps to return the ECU to stock (code 65).

diag_codes.60: EEPROM fault display incl. Power Tuner corrections

notes: Instrument and control functions (Power Tuner app / mode switch) and the self-diagnostic code table, chapter 9.

source.name: Yamaha 2024 YZ250FX Owner's Service Manual (BAJ-2819U-14)

statement: Aftermarket full exhaust systems for the a tester are sold as fitting the 2019-on bikes, the 2024 included (shared with the YZ250F of the same years); they are sold for closed-course competition use only and the maker gives no measured power figure.
notes: Fitment from the retailer listing; other makers (GPR, Yoshimura) list 2020-2024 a tester systems. No 2024 FX before/after dyno found.

source.name: Cycle Gear product listing, Big Gun EXO-R full system YZ250F/YZ250FX

statement: For 2022 the YZ250FX got a new, more direct intake, a new exhaust camshaft, YZ-style brakes (stronger front, lighter rear with a 5 mm smaller rotor) and the YZ250F frame with off-road engine mounts; testers felt it more nimble with slightly less stability.
notes: Manufacturer changes as reported in a first-impression test.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First Impression: 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX

statement: Testers found strong low-end torque that lets it lug and recover from too high a gear, mid-range among the strongest in class, and top end competitive with the highest-revving 250Fs; 3rd-6th gaps were improved so it needs less revving.
notes: Stock bike, first impression.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First Impression: 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX

statement: The 2022 fork felt firm early and rode high in the stroke; softening it with the clickers helped. The shock felt softer than the fork, and clicker plus high-speed compression changes improved the balance.
notes: No clicker counts or sag published.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First Impression: 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX

statement: Yamaha lists 77.0 mm bore x 53.6 mm stroke (250 cc), 13.8:1 compression, DOHC 4 titanium valves and Mikuni fuel injection with a 44 mm throttle body.
notes: Same figures on a magazine 2024/2025/2026 pages and on the 2025 YZ250FX spec (a magazine). Titanium valves stated on the FX spec.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling, 2024 Yamaha YZ250F first look and specs

statement: Fuel is delivered by a high-pressure electric pump through a 12-hole Denso injector into the 44 mm throttle body.
notes: 2019 sources describe the 12-hole injector arriving with the Mikuni throttle body (Keihin before 2019).

source.name: Yamaha Motor USA, 2025 YZ250F features page

statement: The 2024-on cam chain is 10.2 mm wide instead of 8.25 mm and changes from a 4x3 to a 3x2 link construction; cam and crank sprockets are 1.5 mm wider and the tensioner and guides are widened.
notes: A magazine 2024 shootout says this addresses past cam-chain issues. The 2025 YZ250FX shares the beefier chain (a magazine GNCC test).

source.name: Motocross Action, race test of the 2024 Yamaha YZ250F

statement: The clutch is a cable-operated, large-diameter 15-plate wet clutch; testers say it gets hot and needs free-play adjustment during a moto.
notes: Heat/free-play note from a magazine 2024 launch and a magazine 2021 race test. 2027 moves to hydraulic.

source.name: Yamaha Motor USA, 2025 YZ250F features page

topic: Power Tuner app: what it is and how it talks to the bike
statement: The Power Tuner app is free for iOS and Android and connects wirelessly (Wi-Fi from the bike's Communication Control Unit, CCU) to the bike's CAN-bus. It adjusts air/fuel mixture and ignition timing, sets traction and launch control, runs a lap timer, keeps a race log and shows diagnostics, maintenance and engine run time.

notes: Yamaha US 2025 YZ450F page. CCU named on Yamaha's Power Tuner page (placement of CCU affects signal). WR models in the US need a GYTR CCU accessory (see GYTR records).

notes: Listing text applies to the current app (2026). Grid breakpoints for 2023+ bikes are not stated by Yamaha; see the throttle-axis and breakpoint records.

source.name: Powersports Business, Yamaha launches updated Power Tuner App for 2023 YZ450F (Yamaha press release)

topic: Handlebar map switch and number of maps
statement: The ECU holds two maps selectable on the fly with the left handlebar map button (light off = map 1, light lit = map 2); the app ships with three preloaded engine maps and any saved map can be sent into either slot.

vals.indicator: map 1 light off, map 2 light on

notes: YZ250F got new push-button map switchgear for 2024; YZ450F 2023.

source.name: Powersports Business, Yamaha launches updated Power Tuner App for 2023 YZ450F (Yamaha press release)

statement: Yamaha says on the FX models map 1 is the more responsive, quicker-revving map and map 2 is smoother and slower-revving for low traction.
notes: YZ250FX 2024 page gives the same split (aggressive/high traction vs smoother/low traction).

source.name: Yamaha Motor USA, 2024 YZ450FX features page

topic: Fuel vs ignition rule of thumb
statement: Testers summarize that fuel mostly affects traction/torque feel and ignition mostly affects throttle response; the tool changes power character more than peak power.
notes: Same 'fuel = torque, ignition = responsiveness' heuristic repeated by owners on a magazine (2025).

source.name: Dirt Bike Test, GYTR Power Tuner product test

topic: Safety limits: lean mixtures and too much advance
statement: Going too far either way can make the engine run rich, lean or sluggish, or cause detonation (too much advance/too lean). Yamaha builds protections into the app against overly aggressive settings, and the per-cell limits cap how far a rider can go.

vals.protections: built-in limits on aggressive settings (per MXA)

notes: A magazine (Apr 2023) reports the built-in protections. No Yamaha statement on octane/fuel requirements for advanced maps was found.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test, GYTR Power Tuner product test

statement: The app tracks engine run time and has programmable service reminders for engine oil, oil filter and piston, with intervals the owner can edit.
notes: Yamaha confirms maintenance monitoring, engine run time and programmable reminders; item list from a magazine 2025. The 2018 app had multiple running-hour trip meters (AMCN).

source.name: Vital MX, How to use the Yamaha Power Tuner app in detail (Steven Tokarski)

statement: The race log saves settings with track conditions; FAQ-style engine and suspension guides (suspension guide developed with KYB) suggest changes from a chosen symptom.
notes: Yamaha global page describes picking simple prompts to narrow a problem and getting a suggested fix.

source.name: Powersports Business, Yamaha launches updated Power Tuner App for 2023 YZ450F (Yamaha press release)

statement: Maps can be saved, shared with other app users and downloaded as presets; riders also share maps as screenshots on forums, which means copying fuel, ignition and TH% values by hand.
notes: A magazine 2025 notes community maps on a magazine, a magazine and Reddit, e.g. one for Mammoth Mountain at 8,000 ft.
